title: Monstera deliciosa
wikitext: {{Short description|Species of plant}} {{Speciesbox | image = Monstera deliciosa2.jpg | image_caption = Specimen at [[Longwood Gardens]], Pennsylvania | image2 = Costela-de-adão, Monstera deliciosa, em Bagé-RS, Brasil - 55401301647.jpg | image2_caption = Leaf in Brazil | genus = Monstera | species = deliciosa | authority = [[Frederik Michael Liebmann|Liebm.]] | synonyms_ref = {{cite web |url=http://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:87478-1#synonyms |title=''Monstera deliciosa'' Liebm. |author= |date=2017 |website=Plants of the World Online |publisher=Board of Trustees of the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew |access-date=11 November 2020 }} | synonyms = {{Collapsible list| *''Monstera borsigiana'' K.Koch *''Monstera deliciosa'' var. ''borsigiana'' Engl. *''Monstera deliciosa'' var. ''sierrana'' G.S.Bunting *''Philodendron anatomicum'' Kunth & C.D.Bouché *''Philodendron pertusum'' Kunth & C.D.Bouché *''Tornelia fragrans'' Gutierrez ex Schott }}}} '''''Monstera deliciosa''''', the '''Swiss cheese plant''' or '''split-leaf philodendron''',{{cite web |last1=Nosowitz |first1=Dan |title=Monstera and Split-Leaf Philodendron: Is There a Difference Between the Two? |url=https://www.bhg.com/gardening/houseplants/projects/monstera-and-split-leaf-philodendron-difference/ |website=Better Homes & Gardens |access-date=2 February 2022}} is a species of [[flowering plant]]. The common name "Swiss cheese plant" is also used for the related species from the same genus, ''[[Monstera adansonii]]''.{{cite book |last1=Wiersema |first1=John H. |last2=León |first2=Blanca |title=World Economic Plants: A Standard Reference |date=2016 |publisher=CRC Press |isbn=9781466576810 |page=452 |edition=2nd |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=AIrNBQAAQBAJ&pg=PA452 |via=[[Google Books]]}} The common name "split-leaf philodendron" is also used for the species ''[[Philodendron bipinnatifidum]]''. ''Monstera deliciosa'' is native to [[tropical forests]] of southern [[Mexico]], south to [[Panama]]. It has been introduced to many tropical areas, and considered a low-to-moderate invasion risk in [[Hawaii]], [[Seychelles]], [[Ascension Island]] and the [[Society Islands]].{{Cite web |title=Monstera deliciosa (Araceae) |url=http://www.hear.org/species/monstera_deliciosa/ |access-date=2026-05-06 |website=www.hear.org}} It is very widely grown in [[temperate climate|temperate]] zones as a [[houseplant]]. Although the plant contains insoluble [[calcium oxalate]] crystals, which cause a needlelike sensation when touched, the ripe fruit is edible. ==Names== The [[Botanical name#Binary name|specific epithet]] ''deliciosa'' means "delicious", referring to the edible fruit. The genus ''[[Monstera]]'' is named from the [[Latin]] word for "monstrous" or "abnormal", and refers to the unusual [[leaf|leaves]] with natural holes that members of the genus have.{{cite book|title=CRC World Dictionary of Plant Names|volume=3 M-Q|first=Umberto|last=Quattrocchi|publisher=[[CRC Press]]|year=2000 |isbn=978-0-8493-2677-6|page=1723}} Its popular name as a [[houseplant]] of "Swiss cheese plant", or just "cheese plant", is commonly stated to refer to the "eyes" or holes that develop in its leaves similar to the holes in some [[Swiss-type cheese]]s such as [[Emmental cheese]].{{Cite web |title=Oxford University Plants 400: Monstera deliciosa |url=https://herbaria.plants.ox.ac.uk/bol/plants400/Profiles/MN/Monstera |access-date=2026-05-06 |website=herbaria.plants.ox.ac.uk}} Other common names include '''delicious monster''', '''fruit salad plant''', '''fruit salad tree''' (in reference to its edible fruit, which tastes similar to a fruit salad),[http://www.daleysfruit.com.au/fruit%20pages/monstero.htm Daleys Fruit Tree Nursery, Kyogle, New South Wales, ''Monstera'' Fruit Salad Tree]. '''ceriman''' ([[Trinidad]]), '''ojal''' ([[Venezuela]]), '''hojadillo''' ([[Colombia]]),{{cite book|title=Historia y dispersión de los frutales nativos del neotrópico|language=es|publisher=CIAT|first= Víctor Manuel|last= Patiño|date=2002 |page=293|isbn=9586940373}} '''monster fruit''', '''monsterio delicio''', '''monstereo''', '''Mexican [[breadfruit]]''', '''windowleaf, balazo''' and '''[[Mount Penglai|Penglai]] banana'''.{{Cite book |last=Bartholomew |first=Terese Tse |url=http://archive.org/details/isbn_9780939117109 |title=The charming Cicada studio : masterworks by Chao Shao-an |last2=Zhao |first2=Shao'ang |last3=Lee |first3=So Kam Ng |last4=Gao |first4=Meiqing |last5=Asian Art Museum of San Francisco |date=1997 |publisher=San Francisco, CA : Asian Art Museum of San Francisco |others=Internet Archive |isbn=978-0-939117-10-9}} The names in Spanish ({{lang|es|costilla de Adán}}), Portuguese ({{lang|pt|costela-de-adão}}), and French ({{lang|fr|plante gruyère}}) refer to the change of the leaves from [[entire leaf|entire]] to [[wikt:fenestrated#Adjective|fenestrated]], comparing it in the first two cases with the ribs of [[Adam]] and in the third with the hole-filled [[:fr:Gruyère français|gruyère cheese]]. In Mexico, the plant is sometimes referred to as {{lang|es|piñanona}}. In coastal regions of [[Sicily]], especially [[Palermo]], it is called ''zampa di leone'' (lion's paw).{{Cite news |date=2008-08-09 |title=Monstera deliciosa - Monaco Nature Encyclopedia |url=https://www.monaconatureencyclopedia.com/monstera-deliciosa/?lang=en |access-date=2026-05-06 |work=Monaco Nature Encyclopedia |language=en-US}} ==Description== [[File:Monstera Deliciosa at Cox’s Bazar.jpg|thumb|At [[Cox's Bazar]], Bangladesh|333x333px]] This member of the [[arum]] family ([[Araceae]]) is a [[hemiepiphyte]]{{cite web | url=http://www.botmuc.de/en/audio_tour/305.html | website=[[Botanical Garden München-Nymphenburg]] | title=''Monstera'': A hemi-epiphyte}} with [[aerial roots]]. It is able to grow up to {{convert|20|m|ft|abbr=on}} high in the wild, with large, leathery, glossy, [[pinnate]], [[heart-shaped]] leaves {{convert|25|–|90|cm|in|round=0.5|abbr=on}} long by {{convert|25|–|75|cm|in|round=0.5|abbr=on}} broad. The leaves on young plants are smaller and entire with no lobes or holes, but soon produce lobed and [[Leaf shape|fenestrate]] leaves as they grow.http://www.hort.purdue.edu/newcrop/morton/ceriman.html ''Fruits of warm climates'' pp. 15–17 (1987) access date 2010-07-09{{Cite journal |date=1850 |title=Videnskabelige meddelelser fra den Naturhistoriske forening i Kjöbenhavn |url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/bibliography/7547 |journal=Naturhistoriske forening i Kjøbenhavn |via=Harvard University, Museum of Comparative Zoology, Ernst Mayr Library}} Although it can grow very tall in nature, it only measures between {{cvt|2|and|3|m|ft}} when grown indoors. The older the plant, the more the leaves are covered with its familiar large perforations. The exact purpose of the fenestrations remains unclear, but three main theories{{Cite journal |last=Lubenow |first=Cassie |date=2011-05-01 |title=The adaptive function of leaf fenestrations in Monstera spp (Araceae) a look at water, wind, and herbivory, May 2011 |url=https://digitalcommons.usf.edu/tropical_ecology/79/ |journal=Monteverde Institute: Tropical Ecology and Conservation}} have been brought forth: increasing water absorption, limiting the damage done by the wind and reducing the impact of herbivores.{{Cite journal |last=Muir |first=Christopher D. |year=2013 |title=How Did the Swiss Cheese Plant Get Its Holes? |url=https://www.journals.uchicago.edu/doi/10.1086/668819 |journal=The American Naturalist |language=en |volume=181 |issue=2 |pages=273–281 |doi=10.1086/668819 |issn=0003-0147 |url-access=subscription }}{{Cite journal |last=Zheng |first=Jian |last2=Chen |first2=Fengying |last3=Wang |first3=Zhi |last4=Cao |first4=Hong |last5=Li |first5=Xiaoying |last6=Deng |first6=Xin |last7=Soppe |first7=Wim J. J. |last8=Li |first8=Yong |last9=Liu |first9=Yongxiu |year=2012 |title=A novel role for histone methyltransferase KYP/SUVH4 in the control of Arabidopsis primary seed dormancy |url=https://nph.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/j.1469-8137.2011.03969.x |journal=New Phytologist |language=en |volume=193 |issue=3 |pages=605–616 |doi=10.1111/j.1469-8137.2011.03969.x |issn=0028-646X |url-access=subscription }} Wild seedlings grow towards the darkest area they can grow until they find a tree trunk, then start to grow up towards the light, creeping up the tree.[https://web.archive.org/web/20071012225423/http://florawww.eeb.uconn.edu/acc_num/198500876.html Online reference to ''Monstera deliciosa'']{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Kej6HDDMr5o |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211222/Kej6HDDMr5o |archive-date=2021-12-22 |url-status=live|title=Monstera deliciosa Flowers and Fruits HD 03|last=LaboratorTEBA|date=14 February 2014|via=YouTube}}{{cbignore}} The [[inflorescence]] is adorned with a cream-white [[spathe]] of uniform, velvety appearance, covering, like a hood, a yellowish white [[spadix (botany)|spadix]] {{cvt|10|to|15|cm|in}} high and about {{cvt|3|cm|in}} in diameter. Flowers are bisexual, containing both [[androecium]] and [[gynoecium]], though [[Protogyny|protogynous]] development reduces [[self-pollination]]; in the wild they are pollinated mainly by [[Nitidulidae|nitidulid beetles]].{{Cite journal |last=Prieto |first=Danyi |last2=Cascante-Marín |first2=Alfredo |year=2017 |title=Pollination by nitidulid beetles in the hemi-epiphytic aroid Monstera lentii (Araceae: Monsteroideae) |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0367253017331997 |journal=Flora |language=en |volume=231 |pages=57–64 |doi=10.1016/j.flora.2017.04.010 |issn=0367-2530 |hdl=11056/17271 |hdl-access=free }}{{Cite web|title=Monstera deliciosa -- Swiss cheese plant • Earth.com|url=https://www.earth.com/image/monstera-deliciosa-swiss-cheese-plant/|access-date=2021-06-06|website=Earth.com|language=en}} ===Fruit=== [[File:Monsteradeliciosafruit.jpg|thumb|Fruit growing]] The fruit of ''Monstera deliciosa'' is up to {{cvt|25|cm|in|0}} long and {{cvt|3|-|5|cm}} diameter, and it looks like a green ear of maize covered with hexagonal scales. As the fruit ripens, these scales or platelets fall off the fruit, releasing a strong and sweet scent. The smell has been compared to a combination of pineapples and bananas.{{Cite journal|last=Peppard|first=Terry|year=1992|title=Volatile flavor constituents of ''Monstera deliciosa''|journal=Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry|volume=40|issue=2|pages=257–262|doi=10.1021/jf00014a018|bibcode=1992JAFC...40..257P }} The fruit is edible and safe for humans.{{Cite journal|last1=Peters|first1=R. E.|last2=Lee|first2=T. H.|year=1977|title=Composition and physiology of ''Monstera deliciosa'' fruit and juice|journal=Journal of Food Science|volume=42|issue=4|pages=1132–1133|doi=10.1111/j.1365-2621.1977.tb12687.x}} Fruits of plants of the [[Araceae]] (Arum family) often contain [[raphide]]s and [[trichosclereid]]s – needle-like structures of calcium oxalate. In ''M. deliciosa,'' unripe fruit containing these needle-like crystalline structures can cause irritation of the mouth.{{Cite journal |last=Coté |first=Gary G. |year=2009 |title=Diversity and distribution of idioblasts producing calcium oxalate crystals in Dieffenbachia seguine (Araceae) |url=https://bsapubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.3732/ajb.0800276 |journal=American Journal of Botany |language=en |volume=96 |issue=7 |pages=1245–1254 |doi=10.3732/ajb.0800276 |issn=0002-9122 |url-access=subscription }} It takes longer than a year for fruits to reach maturity. The fruit first shows signs of ripening by the yellowing of its lowest scales. As it ripens, the starch that was stored in the green fruit is converted to sugar, giving it its sweet flavor. This mechanism is comparable to how banana fruits ripen. The strong odor the fruit produces becomes noticeable when it is half-ripe. As time passes and the fruit continues to ripen, the odor becomes stronger. After it becomes fully ripe, however, the scent deteriorates quickly.{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EUwynW-Tfs8 |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211222/EUwynW-Tfs8 |archive-date=2021-12-22 |url-status=live|title=Fruit of the Swiss Cheese Plant, ''Monstera deliciosa''|last=Gardening at Douentza|date=27 January 2016|via=YouTube}}{{cbignore}} ==Distribution and growth== [[File:Monstera deliciosa3.jpg|thumb|Leaf]] ''Monstera deliciosa'' is native to humid [[tropical forest]]s, in [[lowlands]] and on lower mountains, in the south of [[Mexico]] and also in [[Costa Rica]], [[Guatemala]] and [[Panama]].{{Cite web |title=Monstera deliciosa Liebm. |url=https://npgsweb.ars-grin.gov/gringlobal/taxonomydetail.aspx?id=24556 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200902033134/https://npgsweb.ars-grin.gov/gringlobal/taxonomydetail.aspx?id=24556 |archive-date=2020-09-02 |access-date=2026-05-06 |website=npgsweb.ars-grin.gov |language=en}}{{Cite web |title=Monstera deliciosa |url=https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:87478-1 |access-date=2026-05-06 |website=Plants of the World Online}} The seeds fall to the ground, then the seedlings crawl (negative [[phototropism]]) until they meet a tree on which to attach. The many adjacent roots thus allow the plant to anchor against its new support and reach the [[canopy (biology)|canopy]] light (although it rarely grows in full sun and prefers a light dimmed by the foliage).{{Cite journal |last=Strong |first=Donald R. |last2=Ray |first2=Thomas S. |date=1975-11-21 |title=Host Tree Location Behavior of a Tropical Vine (Monstera gigantea) by Skototropism |journal=Science |volume=190 |issue=4216 |pages=804–806 |doi=10.1126/science.190.4216.804}} Introduced plants can also be found in other parts of North America ([[Florida]]), Asia ([[Malaysia]] and [[India]]), [[Australia]] and the Western [[Mediterranean climate|Mediterranean]] and Atlantic ([[Sicily]], [[Mainland Portugal]], [[Morocco]], [[Madeira]]), also in [[Madagascar]]. ==Cultivation== ''Monstera deliciosa'' is commonly grown outdoors as an [[ornamental plant]] in the tropics and subtropics. The plant requires a lot of space and a rich and loose soil (ideally garden soil and [[compost]] in equal parts). If it grows in the ground it is better to plant it near a tree, where it can climb, if not against a [[Trellis|trellis]]. It is a "moderately greedy plant", in that it needs to be watered just to keep the soil slightly moist.{{Cite web |title=HS1071/HS311: Monstera Growing in the Florida Home Landscape |url=https://edis.ifas.ufl.edu/publication/HS311 |access-date=2026-05-06 |website=edis.ifas.ufl.edu |language=en}} Its [[plant hardiness|hardiness]] is 11 (that is to say the coldest at {{cvt|-1|C|F|disp=or}}). It cannot withstand these temperatures for more than a few hours, but it can live outside in certain temperate regions ([[Mediterranean coast]], [[Brittany]]). A steady minimum temperature of at least {{convert|13|-|15|C|F}} is preferable, allowing continuous growth. Growth ceases below {{convert|10|C|F|abbr=on}} and it is killed by frost. It needs very bright exposure, but not full sun.{{Cite web |title=How to Care for Monstera (Monstera deliciosa) |url=https://botanapp.com/plant/monstera-deliciosa |access-date=2026-05-06 |website=Botan News |language=en}} Forcing a ''M. deliciosa'' to flower outside of its typical tropical habitat proves to be difficult. Specific conditions need to be met for the plant to flower. However, in its tropical and subtropical habitat, the plant flowers easily. In ideal conditions it flowers about three years after planting. The plant can be [[Plant propagation|propagated]] by taking [[Cutting (plant)|cuttings]] of a mature plant or by [[air layering]]. ===Indoor cultivation=== Its architectural qualities, ease of cultivation, and tolerance of a wide range of conditions make it widely cultivated indoors. For this reason it is a popular plant for the home or office throughout the temperate northern hemisphere. It prefers bright indirect light and temperatures of {{convert|20|-|30|C|F|abbr=on}}. It is usually watered when the soil has slightly dried out (after around one or two weeks). It requires a well-draining, peat-based soil to thrive, such as a soil made with [[perlite]] and pieces of bark.{{Cite web |title=How to Grow and Care for ''Monstera Deliciosa'' |url=https://www.thespruce.com/how-to-grow-monstera-deliciosa-5072671 |access-date=2023-01-10 |website=The Spruce |language=en}} Flowering is rare when grown indoors. In the UK ''Monstera deliciosa''{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector – ''Monstera deliciosa''|url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/11192/i-Monstera-deliciosa-i-(F)/Details|access-date=18 December 2018}} and the cultivar 'Variegata'{{cite web|title=RHS Plant Selector – ''Monstera deliciosa'' 'Variegata'|url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/90394/i-Monstera-deliciosa-i-Variegata-(v)/Details|access-date=18 December 2018}} have gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].{{cite web | url= https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf | title = AGM Plants - Ornamental | date = July 2017 | page = 64 | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | access-date = 4 April 2018}} == Toxicity == ''Monstera deliciosa'' is moderately toxic to both cats and dogs because it contains needle-like insoluble [[calcium oxalate]] crystals. These crystals may cause injury to the mouth, tongue, and digestive tract.{{cite book |url=https://www.springer.com/gp/book/9789048186600 |title=Edible Medicinal and Non-Medicinal Plants}} It also causes [[dermatitis]] by direct contact with cat and dog skin.{{cite journal |last1=Severino |first1=L. |year=2009 |title=Toxic plants and companion animals |url=https://cabidigitallibrary.org/doi/10.1079/PAVSNNR20094008 |journal=CABI Reviews |volume=2009 |pages=1–6 |doi=10.1079/PAVSNNR20094008 |url-access=subscription}} == Uses == In those areas where it grows naturally, ''M. deliciosa'' is considered a delicacy due to its sweet and exotic flavor. The fruit may be ripened by cutting it when the first scales begin to lift up and it begins to exude a pungent odor. It is wrapped in a paper bag and set aside until the scales begin popping off. The scales are then brushed off or fall away to reveal the edible flesh underneath. The flesh, which is similar to [[pineapple]] in texture, can be cut away from the core and eaten. It has a fruity taste similar to [[jackfruit]] and [[pineapple]]. The unripe green fruits can irritate the throat and the latex of the leaves and vines can create rashes in the skin, because both contain [[calcium oxalate]]: that is the reason why the fruits have to be consumed when the scales lift up.{{cite web |title=Plantas silvestres alimenticias de uso tradicional en las comunidades de Pacurita, San José de Purre y Guayabal |url=http://www.reuna.unalmed.edu.co/temporales/memorias/especies/Vegetales/63_plantassilvestresalimenticias.htm |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120402102239/http://www.reuna.unalmed.edu.co/temporales/memorias/especies/Vegetales/63_plantassilvestresalimenticias.htm |archive-date=2012-04-02 |access-date=2012-01-30 |publisher=Reuna.unalmed.edu.co}} The black irritant fibers can be swept off with the application of a little citrus juice. The aerial roots have been used as ropes in Peru, and to make baskets in Mexico. In [[Martinique]], the root is used to make a traditional medicine for snakebites. In Mexico, it is used as traditional medicine for the relief of [[arthritis]] symptoms.{{cite book |last1=Morton |first1=Julia F. |title=Fruits of Warm Climates |year=1987 |publisher=Purdue |location=Miami, Florida |isbn=0-9610184-1-0 |pages=15–17 |url=https://hort.purdue.edu/newcrop/morton/ceriman.html |access-date=13 January 2021}} ==Gallery== File:Monstera deliciosa flower.jpg|Inflorescence File:Monstera deliciosa1281872728.jpg|Leaf and inflorescence File:Monstera deliciosa fruit.JPG|Fruit (unripe) File:Monstera deliciosa ripen fruit 01.JPG|Fruit ripening File:Monstera growing into coir pole.jpg|Aerial root growing into a coconut [[coir]] pole File:Dried Monstera Deliciosa Leaf.jpg|Dried adolescent leaf ==References== {{Reflist}} == External links == * {{Commons-inline|italic=on}} {{Taxonbar|from=Q161077}} [[Category:Monstera|deliciosa]] [[Category:House plants]] [[Category:Flora of Central America]] [[Category:Flora of Mexico]] [[Category:Tropical fruit]] [[Category:Epiphytes]] [[Category:Plants described in 1849]] [[Category:Taxa named by Frederik Liebmann]]
